Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 41-year-old man with 2-month history of fatigue, low mood, poor concentration, insomnia, decreased appetite, decreased libido, and exertional dyspnea.  
• Past history of hypothyroidism on thyroxine; adherence and dosing unclear.  
• No suicidal ideation; supportive marital relationship.  

Consistent differential considerations:  
1. Major depressive disorder / adjustment disorder (high likelihood per DDx; symptoms meet multiple DSM-5 criteria; onset temporally related to occupational change).  
2. Sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism (medium likelihood; known condition with overlapping symptoms).  
3. Anemia or other nutritional deficiency (medium-low likelihood; decreased intake and dyspnea).  

Plan discussed: arrange in-person GP review for physical examination and blood tests (TSH, fT4, CBC, iron studies, B12, folate, renal & liver profile, glucose, vitamin D). Consider mental-health screening and support after lab results.  

Management Plan
- Book face-to-face GP appointment within a few days for full physical exam.  
- Order bloods: thyroid profile, FBC, iron, B12, folate, renal, liver, glucose, vitamin D.  
- Review thyroxine dosing and adherence once TFTs available.  
- Consider PHQ-9/GAD-7 screening; offer mental-health referral or counseling depending on results.  
- Safety-net: advise patient to seek urgent help if mood worsens or suicidal thoughts emerge.  
- Follow-up after results to refine diagnosis and management.

2. Sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism – Moderate likelihood: known condition; compatible systemic symptoms; needs TFTs to confirm.  
3. Anemia (iron-deficiency or other) – Low-moderate likelihood: fatigue and exertional dyspnea with reduced intake; will be assessed with CBC/iron studies.
